Worship extends beyond church services to include connection and contribution within Christian community and outreach.
The Samaritans traditionally worshiped on Mount Gerizim, while Jews believed worship should occur in Jerusalem.
Compasses were historically used to determine direction before GPS technology.
A compass uses Earth’s magnetic field to align with the North and South Poles.
Getting lost at sea is considered a primal human fear due to vulnerability and lack of orientation.

assumptions.text: Spiritual orientation requires internal recalibration rather than external tools alone.
God actively seeks individuals who worship in spirit and truth as a core attribute of genuine faith.
True worship involves both emotional engagement (spirit) and cognitive integrity (truth).
The Holy Spirit plays an active role in guiding authentic worship experiences.
Human beings naturally experience disorientation in life, requiring spiritual recentering.
Church services and traditional worship practices are commonly mistaken as the sole expression of worship.
People who identify as ordinary or non-spiritual still have the capacity to engage in meaningful worship.
External actions such as singing, serving, and connecting with others reflect internal devotion when aligned with divine purpose.
Historical metaphors like the compass effectively represent spiritual navigation and moral direction.
Cultural narratives (e.g., films like Cast Away, The Perfect Storm) reinforce collective anxieties about losing direction, making spiritual metaphor relevant.
